title: Capacity projection & fallback plan — Sprint 12 sync (GPU fleet + regions)
content:
Purpose:
This is the working note for Sprint 12 infrastructure sync focused on GPU fleet capacity projection, per-region headroom, and an actionable fallback plan to protect customer SLAs during the upcoming model rollout (estimated week of 2026-04-02).

High-level summary:
- Short-term (next 3 weeks): expected demand spike ~30–40% driven by a large Dedicated onboarding + two hosted customers shifting to 32k context models.
- Current available GPU pool: 420 total GPUs across cloud regions (us-west1: 180, us-east1: 120, eu-west1: 80, ap-southeast1: 40).
- Reservable buffer target: 15% across fleet (~63 GPUs) to handle bursty tails and rollouts. We are currently at ~10% buffer (~42 GPUs).
- Action: Request expedited capacity add for us-west1 (NVIDIA H100-equivalent) of +24 GPUs; temporary rebalancing between regions and tighter autoscaling thresholds to buy time.

Standup / Meeting log (daily snippets):
- 2026-03-09 (Mon) — Planning kickoff
  - Attendees: Marco, Ava, Priya, Liam, SRE on-call (Dana)
  - Notes: Verified demand forecasts from product: Hosted queued requests growth 35% next 30 days. Dedicated onboarding (Customer: Orion Health) will reserve 48 GPU-hours peak per day for first 10 days.
  - Decision: Open capacity add request with cloud procurement. Start a short-lived migration test shifting 8 GPUs from eu-west1 to us-west1.

- 2026-03-10 (Tue) — Fleet validation
  - Tasks: Disk I/O profiling on us-west1 instances (Ava). Validate GPU kernel versions for new quantized model (Priya).
  - Blockers: Two nodes in eu-west1 failing NVLink handshake intermittently; SRE ticket created (JIRA INFRA-349).
  - Outcome: Isolation suggests a failed firmware update — scheduled remediation Tue night.

- 2026-03-11 (Wed) — Regional headroom review
  - Findings: us-east1 auto-scale thresholds saw 18% latency tail increase when batching target > 16. Lowered default batch size and increased concurrency limits temporarily.
  - Decision: Canary rollout plan will use us-east1 for 10% of traffic; fallback route set to us-west1 and eu-west1 with different model quantization.

- 2026-03-12 (Thu) — Fallback plan tabletop
  - Walkthrough: Simulated failure of us-west1 (region outage) via chaos runbook; validated 95th pct latency remained under SLA after re-routing 70% traffic to eu-west1 + degradation policy (lower context length).
  - Missing: Need automated KV-cache warm migration (current approach is cold start fallback causing ~200ms extra per-request).
  - Action: Add KV cache replication ticket (GH#221) to prioritize for next sprint.

- 2026-03-13 (Fri) — Executive sync prep
  - Prep notes: Summarize exposure and mitigations for product execs. Call out Dedicated customer options: soften commitments, propose phased onboarding to smooth spikes.

Capacity numbers & projection (assumptions explicit):
- Baseline throughput per GPU (H100-equivalent): 250 concurrent tokens/sec for 8k contexts (varies by model).
- Forecast demand (next 30 days): Hosted traffic +35% (weighted toward peak hours), Dedicated onboarding adds 0.6 p95 GPU utilization across peak window.
- Required incremental GPUs to maintain latency SLO (95th < 450ms): ~60 additional H100-eq GPUs if no other mitigations applied.
- Mitigations reducing incremental need to ~24 GPUs:
  - Apply more aggressive prefix caching (estimated 12 GPUs saved)
  - Lower default batch size for interactive endpoints during peak (saves 8 GPUs)
  - Conservative quantized variant for fallback (saves 16 GPUs but with quality tradeoff)

Region-specific notes:
- us-west1: Primary for canaries and Dedicated low-latency customers. Constraint: current vendors quoting 3-week lead time. Procurement working on spot pool augmentation.
- us-east1: Best elasticity, but observed higher latency tails at high batching — tune autoscaler to prioritize concurrency over batch size.
- eu-west1: Limited spare capacity; recent firmware rollbacks after NVLink issue reduced available machines by ~10% for 48h. Plan to re-provision from reserve pool.
- ap-southeast1: Small footprint, used only for APAC beta users. Suggest moving non-critical workloads out during the rollout window.

Fallback and routing policy (practical config):
- Policy ruleset (short description):
  1) If region utilization > 85% for >5m, route new requests to next region in list (per-customer routing allowed).
  2) If overall fleet buffer < 8%, enable degraded-mode quantized model + reduced context lengths for non-enterprise customers.
  3) Canary traffic always has hard cap of 12k tokens/min per model variant.
- Implementation owners: Marco (policy config), Priya (model quantization profiles), Ava (autoscaler tuning).

Open action items (owner / due):
- [Ava] Complete us-west1 I/O profiled remediation and confirm NVLink fix (due 2026-03-15).
- [Priya] Finalize quantized fallback variant and quality regression tests (due 2026-03-18).
- [Marco] Submit procurement request for +24 H100-eq in us-west1 and coordinate pricing/lead time (due 2026-03-14).
- [Liam] Implement temporary rebalancing playbook to move 8 GPUs between regions (due 2026-03-16).
- [SRE on-call Dana] Draft runbook for KV-cache migration and cold-start mitigation (due 2026-03-20).

Risks & contingency: 
- Risk: Procurement lead time exceeds 2 weeks -> contingency to throttle non-critical customers and increase pricedisk credits for Dedicated customers.
- Risk: KV-cache migration complexity -> contingency to use warmed shadow traffic for cache priming before cutover.
- Risk: Firmware regressions on older NVLink nodes -> temporary isolation and reprovisioning from reserve images.

Notes to exec: (short)
- We can avoid a mass capacity order by combining software mitigations (caching + batch tuning) and selective procurement. If procurement times are long, we'll need to negotiate phasing with the large Dedicated customer.

Unresolved questions (items to discuss next sync):
- How much leeway can sales accept on onboarding dates for Orion Health? (sales lead: Maya Patel)
- Approve increased budget for temporary reserved capacity during rollout window? (Finance reviewer: Jonah Reed)
- Prioritize KV-cache replication vs. longer-term cache consistency work — tradeoffs on cost and complexity.

Quick checklist before rollout (pre-flight):
- [ ] Procurement order confirmed or fallback plan approved
- [ ] Canary region routing rulesets validated in staging
- [ ] KV-cache priming script ready and smoke-tested
- [ ] Autoscaler thresholds adjusted and monitored for 48h
- [ ] Customer comms drafted for dedicated onboarding phasing

References & links:
- Demand forecast spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1xyz-capacity-proj
- Current infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/218
- Related Jira tickets: JIRA-INFRA-342, JIRA-INFRA-349, JIRA-INFRA-373
- Slack ops thread: #ops-gpu (link above)

Appendix: short simulation notes
- Chaos test on 2026-03-12 simulated 20% region loss: reroute logic held, 95th latency increase +120ms for 15 minutes, then stabilized. Main contributor was KV cold-start; with priming reduced to +40ms in re-run.

-- End working note --
